# 22. Changelog

All notable changes to NNx are documented here. Format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versioning is roughly [SemVer](https://semver.org/) — pre-1.0, we allow behavior changes (typically bug fixes) without renaming public APIs.

This file intentionally keeps the standard Keep a Changelog heading format rather than the hierarchical numbering used by the rest of the documentation.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.4.0](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0) (2026-10-06)

### Added

- **A published feature-composition matrix.** `docs/feature-composition.yaml` (FEAT-039) registers which feature combinations are verified, unsupported or unverified. Each of its 37 scenarios across training controls, checkpoint/resume, model transformations, inference/export, decisions and typed results, and packaging (FEAT-010, -023, -025, -029, -030, -031, -033 and -037 each appear in at least one combination) records its device / dtype / dependency profile, expected boundary, pytest node ids and rationale. `scripts/check_feature_composition.py` validates the schema and unique IDs, collects every node id (a stale reference fails naming its scenario), runs the scenarios with a phase-recording plugin (an import, a skip, an xfail or a setup / teardown failure never verifies), and renders `docs/feature-composition.md` from that evidence report. A report from other sources or another profile renders unverified. A new CI `feature-composition` job gates verified rows and keeps the report; the docs site and wiki render the same report (identical evidence digest). CUDA AMP and ONNX Runtime rows stay unverified on CPU ([#256](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/256)).

- **Decision-model research pilot (experimental, no-go).** `examples/decision_model_pilot.py` (FEAT-023) scores `(state, question, candidate description)` triples with a shared encoder and scalar head registered through `register_model_factory` (no new `Nets` member): Choice decisions softmax the candidates (cross-entropy) and Boolean ones take one logit (binary cross-entropy), both trained; Score is refused. A validated pre-execution manifest (licences, disjoint fit/select/held-out family splits, schemas, seeds, baselines, compute cap, stop rule, model identity, predeclared trade-off) comes first. The offline mechanics mode enforces the compute cap and produces a checkpoint reloaded through the registry, candidate-aligned replay records, trial and stop records, and a no-go report. The empirical mode writes its manifest and reports *blocked*: the resources are not supplied, and the empirical runs are outside this repository. See `docs/decision-model-pilot.md` ([#262](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/262)).

- **Budgeted experiment search through Optuna (`nnx.search`, extra `optuna`).** `search(plan, space, apply=..., monitor=..., budget=SearchBudget(trials=, updates_per_trial=, deadline_seconds=), study_name=, storage=, sampler=, pruner=)` runs a sequential Optuna study in which each trial's parameters become a fresh `ExperimentPlan` via `apply` (the base plan is unchanged; fresh model, optimizer, loaders and callbacks; its own attempt id and run), scored by one validation monitor equal to the plan's own. The space (`FloatParam`, `IntParam`, `CategoricalParam`), budget, monitor and plan are validated before any trial, and a stored study with a different identity is refused. Completed, failed, pruned and orphaned trials all count against the budget. The update cap stops right after the N-th committed update, a deadline starts no trial once expired and stops a running one at its next boundary (recording the overrun), and a trial stopped mid-epoch keeps only its committed epochs. Pruning sees each validated epoch's value at step = epoch; missing or non-finite values fail. A trial's value is its run's monitor decision (the epoch its BEST checkpoint holds). A failed fit is recorded with its message and the search goes on; a configuration error in `apply` stops it. Every `TrialOutcome` keeps parameters, terminal reason, resources, monitor value and attempt / run / checkpoint links, and `SearchResult.best` is the best completed trial. The training loop gains `ctx.update_listeners` and `ctx.stop_at_update` (stop at an update boundary without committing the epoch in progress). `import nnx` never imports Optuna. See `docs/concepts.md` §29 and `examples/search_offline.py` ([#266](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/266)).

- **Single-node data parallelism under `torchrun` (`nnx.distributed`).** `model.train(params, distributed=DDP())` trains over the process group `torchrun` started (`nnx.distributed.init_process_group()`; Gloo on CPU, NCCL with one GPU per rank) through PyTorch's `DistributedDataParallel`, with every committed update equal to one process training on the ranks' union batch: gradients synchronize only at committed updates and are normalized by the global loss denominator (unequal valid counts included), an all-masked global window is skipped everywhere, and non-finite losses, step-count mismatches, preflight refusals and writer-side commit failures fail on every rank together instead of hanging. `train_loader(dataset, batch_size, policy="pad"|"drop", seed=)` partitions each epoch's seeded permutation evenly; `validation_loader` shards rows unpadded so every id is scored exactly once. Records are global and identical on every rank (monitors, early stopping, BEST and schedulers agree) and every rank returns the same run; only the writer rank holds the lease and writes history, checkpoints (canonical keys; world size, partitions and every rank's RNG for a same-world resume) and provenance. Callbacks declare `distributed = "all"` or `"writer"`; `writer_only(factory)` builds a `TensorBoardCallback` / `WandbCallback` on the writer alone. FP32, default steps, one optimizer, one node, no batch normalization. See `docs/architecture.md` §3, `docs/quickstart.md` §3.10 and `examples/ddp_supervised.py` ([#265](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/265)).

- **Opt-in `torch.compile` and bounded benchmarks (`nnx.compilation`, `nnx.benchmarking`).** `model.train(params, compile=CompileSpec(backend="inductor", mode=None, fullgraph=False, dynamic=None, on_failure="error"))` runs the built-in step's FP32 forward (and the fit's validation) through a per-call compiled wrapper beside — never replacing — `model.net`, so checkpoints keep eager keys, optimizers own the eager parameters and export, `summary`, tying and later inference stay eager. Refused up front with a custom step or objective, a graph or custom net, reduced precision or a topology-changing callback (QAT); not for DDP or quantization, and no speedup is guaranteed. `on_failure="eager"` re-runs only the failing forward eagerly (never a partly applied update). `CompileRecord` (requested backend/options/policy/torch version; effective `compiled` with full or partial capture, `eager` with its restart, or `failed`) is on `NNRun.compile`, in `metadata.yaml`, checkpoint training state and `attempt.json`, never in the run id. `benchmark_forward` / `compare_compile` separate first-call compile cost from warmed latency, throughput and dispersion from identical weights; `profile_forward` runs a finite `torch.profiler` schedule into an explicit directory. See `docs/concepts.md` §28 and `examples/benchmark_compile.py` ([#264](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/264)).

- **An opt-in `Result` at fallible boundaries (`nnx.result`).** Frozen `Ok` / `Err` with `map` (only an `Ok`), `map_error` (only an `Err`), `bind` and `recover` (each flattening one `Result` its callback returns; anything else raises `TypeError`) and `unwrap` (raising `UnwrapError` with the typed error). Combinators never catch a callback's exception, and a `Result` has no truth value — `Ok(0)`, `Ok(None)` and `Ok(False)` are successes. Three boundary wrappers convert exactly the exceptions they declare into `Err(BoundaryError(code, where, context, cause))`: `validate_decision_request_result` builds a typed question from plain data (`InvalidDecisionRequest` → `invalid_decision_request`, no provider call), `decide_result` separates a provider failure (`provider_failure` with its request id, `unsupported`) from a successful abstention (an `Ok` of `SelectiveDecision`s, probabilities and reasons kept), and `inspect_bundle_result` delegates to the safe `inspect_bundle` (`artifact_missing`, `bundle_invalid`; never unpickles). Every exception-style API is unchanged. See `docs/decisions.md` §10.1, `docs/concepts.md` §27 and `examples/result_boundaries.py` ([#263](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/263)).

- **Ordered logits pipelines (`nnx.generation.OrderedLogitsPipeline`).** Decoding stages that run exactly in their declared order, beside the canonically sorted `LogitsChain` (unchanged): `OrderedLogitsPipeline.of(LogitsStage.temperature(0.5), LogitsStage.top_p(0.8))` keeps duplicates (two temperature-0.5 stages equal one 0.25) and custom positions, and `append` / `prepend` return new pipelines over immutable `LogitsStage` specs — a processor passed in is copied by value, and every run compiles fresh processors. Values are validated (finite, in domain) when a stage is made; a zero-temperature stage is greedy and terminal, so a stage after it raises instead of being reordered. `generate(logits_pipeline=...)` compiles the pipeline once per call on the cached and uncached paths, with token history, `on_token`, `stop` and seeded output equal to the explicit processor list; passing it with `logits_chain` raises before the model is touched. Built-in pipelines round-trip through `state()` / `from_state()` (`{"version": 1, "stages": [...]}`); a `CustomStage` is runtime-only (its state stays the caller's) unless its tag has a `LogitsStageCodec` registered in-process — data never names code to import, and a pipeline never enters a checkpoint or a run identity. See `docs/lm.md` §5.1 and `examples/ordered_logits_pipeline.py` ([#254](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/254)).

- **Typed decisions on Jev models through the TypeSafe SDK (`nnx.decisions.JevProvider`).** A new `jev` extra (`pip install "thekaveh-nnx[jev]"`, pinned and tested at `typesafe-sdk>=0.7,<0.8`) adapts `Choice`, `Boolean` and `Score` questions to the SDK's `system_one` call: one request per text holding every question (a Choice keyed by its options' descriptions, never their ids; a Score by its levels in order; a Boolean as a `noul`), answers realigned to each question's own order and validated, a Score's expected score in `vendor_score`. Each result's `raw` is plain JSON — the model the service resolved (even for an alias request), the requested model, the request id and reported token usage, absent fields left absent, never clients, headers or credentials. A Choice's or Score's `confidence` is recorded as `provider_confidence`, Jev's own certainty rather than a probability of being correct; a Boolean gets none. The SDK's `RetryPolicy` owns retries and the adapter sends each request once; what still fails becomes `JevTimeout`, `JevAuthenticationError`, `JevRateLimited` (with `retry_after_ms`), `JevMalformedResponse` or `JevError`, all `ProviderFailure`s keeping the SDK error as `__cause__` and the service's `request_id`, through a decision job (`JobFailed.__cause__`) or the benchmark (a record's `reason`) too. Injected sync / async clients stay the caller's, and the provider never builds a second client beside one (a sync-only provider has no async methods, so a decision job runs it in its own worker thread); clients it builds itself close on `with` (sync) / `async with` (both) exit, after an error or cancellation too. Each text is one request, so call budgets count provider calls, not requests — bound them with `max_batch`. `import nnx` never imports the SDK, and a provider that would need it raises `ImportError` naming the extra. `scripts/smoke_jev_live.py` is an opt-in live smoke pinned to `jev-1.13.0`. See `docs/decisions.md` §6 and `examples/decision_jev.py` ([#220](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/220)).

### Changed

- **The vision, graph and plotting stacks are extras (`thekaveh-nnx[vision]`, `[graph]`, `[plots]`; `[domains]` for all three).** torchvision, torch_geometric and Plotly are no longer core dependencies, and `import nnx` loads none of them: the core install trains, predicts, saves and reloads models with torch, NumPy, pandas and scikit-learn alone. Features that need one import it on use and, when it is missing, raise an `ImportError` naming the extra — `NNDataset` (`vision`); the graph nets, `NNGraphDataset`, `Nets.GRAPH_*`, `nnx.graph_tasks` and `nnx.link_tasks` (`graph`); `VisUtils` figures, `nnx.viz` figures and `nnx.lr_finder` (`plots`, which refuses before touching data, model or RNG state). An `ImportError` from inside an installed package keeps its own cause. With the extras installed, flat and deep names, class identity, signatures and `Nets` values are unchanged; `nnx.__all__` lists a domain name only when its extra is installed, so `from nnx import *` works on a core install. Without Plotly, `NNRun`'s notebook repr keeps its table and drops the chart, and `VisUtils.classification_report` still returns a DataFrame. The `viz` extra now pulls Plotly for its figures. **Upgrading:** install `thekaveh-nnx[domains]` to keep the previous dependency set. `scripts/smoke_core_install.py` checks an installed wheel per profile, run by new CI `installed-profiles` and release `artifact-profiles` jobs over the minimum and current torch pairs; the `floor-deps` lane installs `[domains]` ([#249](https://github.com/thekaveh/NNx/issues/249)).
